observations: Reviewer identity: the runtime gave me no task or agent ID, so reviewer.task is null. The parent must supply the real Agent ID from its own tool result. It must not invent one. If none is available, this response cannot be recorded, because the CLI requires reviewer.task.

What I opened myself with Read: the request JSON for 08-1 (full scene, production and cast), assets/characters/pharmacy-lab.png, assets/characters/main-cast.png, assets/panels/07-4.png, assets/panels/08-1.png and workflow/review/page-08.png. I did not open workflow/storyboards/page-08.svg or source/original.txt, so this review does not cover them. Every file I opened was readable.

The Pharmacist matches pharmacy-lab.png. He has short wavy black hair with grey at the temples, kind hooded eyes with crow's feet, thick arched brows, a round face with a neat moustache and dimpled cheeks, a white coat over a light-blue collared shirt, and two blue pens in the breast pocket as on the sheet. He smiles in a careful, reassuring way, which fits the emotion field.

Hands match production. His right hand (viewer's left) holds a plain white unlabelled box and is slipping it into the bag. His left hand (viewer's right) holds the open white paper bag at its edge. The fingers read correctly. The box and bag carry no labels, logos or text. The shelf boxes behind him are plain white.

The tablet stands on its stand in the left foreground with the screen toward the reader. The screen shows one card with a teal capsule icon and two blank bars. There is no drug name, letter or number anywhere in the art. The top-left wall is plain, leaving room for the caption.

From 07-4 to 08-1: in 07-4 Ravi waves goodbye outside the clinic in morning sun. 08-1 is a new place, the pharmacy, and the caption 'Meanwhile' bridges the change. The daylight is consistent and the cut reads as a clear place change.

Lettering on page-08.png: the top-left caption ends just left of his hair (box right edge at about page x 286), so it does not cover his face. The box, bag and both hands are clear. However, the 'NEW PRESCRIPTION' label (about page x 30-262, y 316-420) covers almost the whole tablet. Only the top bezel shows, and the capsule card is hidden. The tablet is the key prop that shows the notification arrived, so the reader loses the visual link. On 08-2, 08-5 and 08-6 the order or results card stays visible next to its label.

issues.problem: In the composite, the 'NEW PRESCRIPTION' label hides almost the whole tablet, including the screen card with the capsule icon. Only the top bezel is visible, so the key prop that shows the notification cannot be read. Move or shrink the label, for example place it on the wall above the tablet or let it cover only the blank bars, so the screen card and the tablet stay readable. Then recheck the composite.

The Lab Technician matches the sheet. She has a neat high bun with loose strands, thin round glasses, large round eyes, thin straight brows, a narrow face with a sharp chin and freckles across the nose, a small stud earring, a light-blue lab coat over a navy top, and purple nitrile gloves.

Hands match production. Her right hand (sleeve from the viewer-left shoulder) holds up one empty purple-capped tube with a blank white label, just picked from the rack. Her left gloved hand rests flat on the counter. The finger count and grip on the tube are plausible.

The monitor in the right foreground is angled toward the reader. It shows one card with three tube icons and two blank bars, with no test names, letters or values. A rack of five empty capped tubes with blank labels stands in the left foreground. The spec places the rack 'beside the monitor', but here it is on the opposite side of the panel. This is minor and does not block. A blue sample-collection chair at the left sets up the room for 08-3. The top wall is plain for the caption.
Her gaze rests on the tube in her hand rather than on the monitor. That still reads as checking the order and picking a tube, which matches production.moment.

On the left, Ravi sits in a blue sample-collection chair. His face matches main-cast.png: short side-parted black hair, trimmed beard, thick straight brows, narrow eyes creased in a smile. He wears the light-green shirt with rolled sleeves. His dark-brown shoulder bag is on his lap. His right hand presses a small white cotton pad to the inner side of his bent left arm near the elbow. His watch is on the left wrist. This matches production.hands. No needle appears anywhere.

On the right, the Lab Technician matches pharmacy-lab.png: bun, round glasses, light-blue coat over navy, purple gloves. She faces Ravi and smiles with her mouth open as she speaks. Her left hand (viewer's right) holds one capped tube with a white label. Her right hand presses a blank white sticker onto it. This matches the production entry 'labtech left holding / right pressing label'.

From 08-2 to 08-3: the room is the same lab. Both panels show the blue collection chair, white counters and cabinets, a tube rack and a monitor with a tube-icon card, so it reads as the same room. Minor note: in 08-2 she picked an empty purple-capped tube, but here the tube in her hand and the three tubes in the rack have red caps and dark-red contents. The monitor icons are red as well. A multi-tube draw makes this plausible, and at this panel size it does not break the reading. I record it as a non-blocking continuity note. The screen and the sticker carry no text, test names or values.

Composition after the edit: both figures sit in the lower half, with a plain wall across the upper half. The caption and balloon now fit above the heads, at the cost of small figures and an empty band of wall between the text and the heads. The faces are small but readable.

Lettering on page-08.png: the caption (about page x 32-448, y 460-565) and the balloon (about x 714-985, y 460-630) both sit above the figures. Ravi's face (about y 630-702) and the Technician's face (about y 600-680) are uncovered, as are both hands, the cotton pad and the tube. The balloon tail runs down-left from the balloon and ends just right of the Technician's head, at about page x 718, y 655. It points clearly at her and not at Ravi.
